title: Cloud Storage Privacy Risk Calculator - Assess Your Data Security
metaDescription: Calculate your cloud storage privacy risk score. Evaluate provider security, encryption, and data protection to keep your files safe from breaches.
description: Assess your cloud storage privacy risks with our comprehensive calculator. Evaluate your provider's security practices, encryption methods, and data protection features to understand how well your files are protected from unauthorized access.

inputs.label: Can Your Provider Open Your Files?

options.label: Yes, it holds the keys (standard cloud storage)
Only some: my sensitive files are in an end-to-end encrypted folder

inputs.helpText: End-to-end (zero-knowledge) encrypted storage locks files on your device, so the provider can't open them

inputs.helpText: What type of data do you primarily store?

inputs.helpText: Do you use any encryption beyond the provider's default? It only lowers your score for files the provider could otherwise open.

outputFields.label: Privacy Risk Score
outputFields.description: Overall privacy risk assessment (0-100, lower is better)

outputFields.label: Primary Recommendation
outputFields.description: Most important step to improve your privacy

formula: const accessScores = { 'can-read': 60, 'partly': 35, 'cannot': 15, 'unsure': 65 }; const sensitivity = { 'personal': 1, 'creative': 1.1, 'business': 1.2, 'legal': 1.3, 'financial': 1.4, 'medical': 1.5 }; const encryptionReduction = { 'none': 0, 'manual': -25, 'zero-knowledge': -30, 'third-party': -20 }; const sharingScores = { 'never': 0, 'rare': 5, 'occasional': 10, 'frequent': 20, 'daily': 30 }; const e2eLevel = accessScores['cannot']; const exposure = Math.max(e2eLevel, (accessScores[providerAccess] ?? 65) + (encryptionReduction[encryptionUsed] ?? 0)); const sharing = sharingScores[sharingFrequency] ?? 10; let points = exposure + sharing; if (!twoFactor) points += 15; if (dataAmount > 100) points += 5; if (dataAmount > 500) points += 10; const riskScore = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, Math.round(points * (sensitivity[dataTypes] ?? 1)))); let riskLevel; if (riskScore <= 25) riskLevel = 'Low Risk'; else if (riskScore <= 50) riskLevel = 'Moderate Risk'; else if (riskScore <= 75) riskLevel = 'High Risk'; else riskLevel = 'Critical Risk'; const ownEncryption = (encryptionReduction[encryptionUsed] ?? 0) < 0; const providerStep = { 'can-read': ownEncryption ? 'Make sure every sensitive file is encrypted before upload, with your own tool or a zero-knowledge option from your provider: the provider can open anything uploaded unencrypted.' : 'Move sensitive files to end-to-end encrypted storage, or encrypt them on your device before upload.', 'partly': 'Check that every sensitive file is inside your end-to-end encrypted folder, copies included, or encrypt the rest before upload.', 'unsure': 'Find out whether your provider can open your files (look for end-to-end or zero-knowledge encryption in its security settings); if it can, make sure every sensitive file is encrypted before upload.' }; const twoFactorStep = 'Turn on two-factor authentication, with an authenticator app rather than SMS.'; const steps = [[exposure - e2eLevel, providerStep[providerAccess] ?? providerStep['unsure']], [twoFactor ? 0 : 15, twoFactorStep], [sharing, 'Share with named people rather than open links, set links to expire, and remove shares you no longer need.']]; const top = steps.reduce((best, step) => (step[0] > best[0] ? step : best)); let recommendation; if (top[0] <= 0) recommendation = 'Keep 2FA on, and review which apps and devices can reach your account from time to time.'; else recommendation = top[1] + (!twoFactor && top[1] !== twoFactorStep ? ' Turn on two-factor authentication as well.' : ''); return { riskScore, riskLevel, recommendation };

educational.methodology: This calculator adds up what could expose your files: a provider that can open them, no two-factor authentication, frequent sharing and a large archive. Encryption you add counts only for files your provider could otherwise open. The total is then scaled up for more sensitive data, by up to 1.5 times for medical records. Scores range from 0-100, with lower scores indicating better privacy protection.
tips: Use zero-knowledge encrypted providers like Proton Drive or Tresorit for sensitive data
Always enable two-factor authentication on your cloud storage accounts
Encrypt sensitive files locally before uploading to any cloud service
Regularly review and revoke sharing permissions for old files and folders
Review which apps and devices can access your cloud account, and remove the ones you no longer use
